cars.specification_market: Japan eighth-generation Galant / Legnum VR-4 road programme introduced in August 1996, represented by the Galant saloon. Selected engine reference is Mitsubishi’s historical 6A1-series account: 6A13 nominal 2.5-litre DOHC twin-turbo intercooled V6, 280 PS and 37.0 kgf-m. The year denotes programme introduction, not proof that every 1996 trim had this output. No gearbox or individual trim is assigned: a separate factory model retrospective describes a 280-PS automatic, while launch-manual/automatic differences require a dated catalogue before combining them. AYC is family-level historical significance, not a claim that all grades have it. Group Galant and derived Legnum, manual/automatic, Type S/Type V, Super VR-4, facelift and years within this one generation. Not the earlier E39A four-cylinder rally road family, 1992 V6 generation, ordinary GDI Galant, Aspire or US-market GTZ. No exact cc, peak rpm, acceleration, mass, dimensions, brakes, tyres, fuel injection, later S-AWC/ACD/Super AYC or all-grade standard equipment inferred.
cars.summary: The eighth-generation Galant / Legnum VR-4 road family belongs for its place in the 1996 production introduction of Mitsubishi’s Active Yaw Control, using left-right rear-wheel torque transfer to influence cornering. A manufacturer engineering paper documents that chassis milestone. Its V6 twin-turbo sporting lineage is distinct from the earlier four-cylinder rally Galant; bodies, trims and years count once.

sources.notes: Complete relevant 6A1-series section read, including the August 1996 Galant/Legnum introduction and selected 280-PS 6A13 engine description. The section is filed under 1991 engine-family introduction; that is not the Galant launch date. Family-wide engine years, production totals and displacement range do not become VR-4 figures. Selected engine values only; no gearbox/trim combination inferred.

sources.title: Car History — eighth-generation Galant and derived Legnum, 1996 sections
sources.notes: Complete relevant Galant and Legnum prose and displayed generic dimensions read. Establishes generation, wagon derivation and full-time viscous-coupled 4WD. Generic dimensions and ordinary GDI technology are not imported into the VR-4. Its 280-PS INVECS-II automatic description is not treated as an exact 1996 launch specification. AYC/ASC are specified for certain Galant trims; the Legnum account separately describes AYC on VR-4 and ASC/TCL on Type S. Do not collapse these into universal equipment.

sources.publisher: Mitsubishi Motors Corporation; mirrored by MMC Manuals
sources.title: Technology DNA of MMC — Hashimoto, Fukuyama, Oikawa and Kume, Technical Review 2005, printed pp. 8–9
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer engineering paper, preserved facsimile
sources.notes: Paper heading/authors and complete vehicle-dynamics section read as web PDF text, especially printed pages 8–9 / PDF indices 9–10. Explicitly dates Galant and Lancer Evolution AYC application to 1996 and explains torque difference between left/right rear wheels. Admission evidence for the concrete production chassis milestone; no unqualified worldwide priority claim, claim of independent road testing, all-trim availability or complete 90-page visual review. Earlier 1987 ECS/4WS and later Evo MR aluminium roof are kept separate from this VR-4 reference.
